statement.p: Using Riemann sums with four subdivisions in each direction, find upper and lower bounds for the volume under the graph of f(x,y) = 7+3xy above the rectangle R with 0\le x\le 2,\quad 0\le y \le 5.

static.solution:
R into subrectangles with the lines x=0, x=0.5, x=1, x=1.5, and x=2 and the lines y=0, y=1.25, y=2.5, y=3.75, and y=5. Then we have 16 subrectangles, each of which we denote R_{(a,b)}, where (a,b) is the location of the lower-left corner of the subrectangle.
We want to find a lower bound and an upper bound for the volume above each subrectangle. The lower bound for the volume of R_{(a,b)} is 0.625 ( \mbox{Min of } f \mbox{ on } R_{(a,b)}) because the area of R_{(a,b)} is 0.5\cdot 1.25=0.625. The function f(x,y) = 7+3xy increases with both x and y over the whole region R. Thus, \mbox{Min of } f \mbox{ on } R_{(a,b)} = f(a,b) = 7+3ab, because the minimum on each subrectangle is at the corner closest to the origin.
Similarly, \mbox{Max of } f \mbox{ on } R_{(a,b)} = f(a+0.5,b+1.25) = 7 + 3(a+0.5)(b+1.25). So we have \mbox{Lower sum } = \sum_{(a,b)} 0.625(7+3ab) = 0.625 \sum_{(a,b)} 7+3ab = 70 + 0.625\sum_{(a,b)}3 ab Since a=0, 0.5, 1, 1.5 and b= 0, 1.25, 2.5, 3.75, expanding this sum gives \mbox{Lower} = 70 + 0.625 (0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 1.875 + 3.75 + 5.625 + 0 + 3.75 + 7.5 + 11.25 + 0 + 5.625 + 11.25 + 16.875) = 112.188.
Similarly, we can compute the upper sum: \mbox{Upper sum }= \sum_{(a,b)}0.625(7+3(a+0.5)(b+1.25)) = 0.625\sum_{(a,b)}(7+3(a+0.5)(b+1.25)) = 70 + 0.625\sum_{(a,b)}(a+0.5)(b+1.25) = 187.188.
